issues.failure_explanation: The triangle inequality (triangle) splits the error into a first term bounded by $ε\|f\|_D$ (from $\|\wh{\Aa}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|\leq\varepsilon$) and a second term bounded by $C\varepsilon\|\Aa\|\|f\|$ (from Corollary order corollary). The total is $(1+C\|\Aa\|)\|f\|_D\varepsilon$, which strictly exceeds the claimed bound $\|\Aa\|\|f\|_D\varepsilon$ whenever $\|\Aa\|\leq 1$ (as the paper establishes). The proof writes $\lesssim$ but the statement asserts $\leq$ with constant exactly $\|\Aa\|$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase the constant in the conclusion to $K\|f\|_D\varepsilon$ for some constant $K>\|\Aa\|$ (e.g. $K=1+C\|\Aa\|$ where $C$ is the convergence-rate constant from Corollary order corollary).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit error bound $\|\wh{\Aa}_{NM}P_{D_N}f-\Aa f\|\leq\|\Aa\|\|f\|_D\varepsilon$ in Theorem OC theorem and its noise analogue Theorem OC theorem noise is not established. The qualitative $O(\varepsilon)$ rate with probability $\geq p$ survives.
issues.title: OC theorem error bound constant is too tight
issues.why_classification: A single constant change in the conclusion preserves the qualitative rate, probability guarantee, and method. No new lemma or construction is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own FEM example, $N = O(h^{-d})$ so $h^{-1} = O(N^{1/d})$. For $d=1$ this gives $h^{-1} = O(N)$, not $O(N^{1/2})$. The stated scaling $O(N^{1/2})$ corresponds to $d=2$. Consequently the derived rate $M=O(\varepsilon^{-2-2/\alpha})$ and cost $C(\varepsilon,p)=O(\varepsilon^{-2-3/\alpha})$ are wrong for 1D, and the conclusion 'This is equal to the cost in the previous example' does not hold for 1D (the correct cost is $O(\varepsilon^{-2-5/\alpha})$).

failure_location.quote: for example for a $1$-dimensional FEM basis $\norm{\bm{G}_N^{-1}}= \Oo\qty(h_N^{-1})= \Oo\left(N^{\nicefrac12} \right)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change '1-dimensional' to '2-dimensional' so that $h_N^{-1}=O(N^{1/2})$ and the cost comparison are correct. Alternatively, keep 1D but correct the scaling to $O(N)$ and revise the cost comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate and cost-comparison claims in the second illustrative example after Theorem OC theorem are wrong for the stated 1D setting.
issues.title: FEM example gives wrong scaling of ‖G_N^{-1}‖ for 1D
issues.why_classification: The least severe repair (one-word dimension change) preserves the example's conclusion. The main theorems are unaffected. However, two different repairs are possible (change dimension or change scaling), so this is not a pure typo.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The random variables $\set{(\bm{\eta}_N^m, \bm{\xi}_N^m)}_{m=1}^M$ have mean $\bm{0}$, are symmetric, independent, and independent of $\set{\bm{x}_m }_{m=1}^M$.

issues.failure_explanation: The noisy vector $\bm{g}=\Psi_N(x)+\bm{\eta}$ includes additive noise, so $E[\bm{g}\bm{g}^\dagger]=G_N+E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger]\neq G_N$ when the noise covariance is nonzero. The proof asserts $G_N=E[\bm{g}\bm{g}^\dagger]$ and uses this to apply Bernstein's inequality, which bounds $\|\tilde{G}_{NM}-G_N^{\text{noisy}}\|$ rather than $\|\tilde{G}_{NM}-G_N^{\text{clean}}\|$. Consequently the estimator $\tilde{A}_{NM}=\tilde{C}_{NM}\tilde{G}_{NM}^{+}$ converges to $C_N(G_N+E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger])^{-1}\neq C_N G_N^{-1}=\Aa_N$, so the error has a non-vanishing bias. For instance with $N=1$, $\psi_1(x)=x$, $\Aa=\mathrm{Id}$, Gaussian noise variance $\sigma^2$: the estimator converges to $(1+\sigma^2)^{-1}$ instead of $1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a bias correction term to the bound: $\|\tilde{A}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|\leq C\delta+\|C_N\|\|(G_N+E[\bm{\eta}\bm{\eta}^\dagger])^{-1}-G_N^{-1}\|$. This preserves the sampling-error analysis but weakens the conclusion: the error no longer vanishes as $M\to\infty$.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition noise bound and Theorem OC theorem noise claim $\|\tilde{A}_{NM}-\Aa_N\|\leq C\delta$ (or $\leq\varepsilon$), but the left side converges to a positive bias as $M\to\infty$. The advertised convergence to $\Aa_N$ with noisy data is false. Example noise example 1's claim about noise resilience is also unreliable.
issues.title: Noise analysis identifies noisy expectations with clean matrices, creating unaccounted bias
issues.why_classification: Every complete resolution either adds a bias term (changing the central guarantee from vanishing error to bounded error) or requires a new debiasing construction absent from the source. The promised convergence of the noisy estimator to the clean Galerkin projection is a central guarantee of the noise section and is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: From the source, $\sigma^{-2}|\bm{\eta}_N|^2\sim\chi^2_N$ and $\sigma^{-2}|\bm{\xi}_N|^2\sim\chi^2_N$ independently, so $\sigma^{-2}|(\bm{\eta}_N,\bm{\xi}_N)|^2=\sigma^{-2}(|\bm{\eta}_N|^2+|\bm{\xi}_N|^2)\sim\chi^2_{2N}$. The probability of interest is $P[\chi^2_{2N}\leq\gamma_N]=F_{2N}(2N)\approx 1/2$. The paper instead computes $1-F_N(\gamma_N)=P[\chi^2_N>2N]\leq(2/e)^{N/2}\approx 0$, confusing $\chi^2_N$ with $\chi^2_{2N}$ and inverting the inequality. The claimed $\tilde{p}_N\geq 1-(2/e)^{N/2}\approx 1$ is wrong; the correct value is $\approx 1/2$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $F_N(\gamma_N)$ with $F_{2N}(\gamma_N)$ (the CDF of $\chi^2_{2N}$ at $2N$) and use an appropriate tail bound. The qualitative conclusion that the noise effect is manageable survives, but $\tilde{p}_N\approx 1/2$ rather than $\approx 1$.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed value $\tilde{p}_N\approx 1$ is wrong ($\approx 1/2$), so the conclusion that noise has small effect (factor 2) understates the noise impact in the sample-complexity bound's logarithmic factor.
issues.title: Noise example computes wrong chi-squared tail probability
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the distribution and probability computation preserves the example's qualitative message. The quantitative conclusion changes by a factor of about 2 but no main theorem is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption projection assumption gives $\|(P_{F_N}-I)\phi\|_F\to 0$ for each fixed $\phi\in F$, but the proof applies it to $\phi=\Aa f_{N_i}$, which varies with $N_i$. Since $f_{N_i}\stackrel{w}{\to}f$ only weakly in $D$ (infinite-dimensional), $\|f_{N_i}-f\|_D\not\to 0$ and hence $\|\Aa f_{N_i}-\Aa f\|_F\not\to 0$ in general. The claimed limit $(I-P_{F_{N_i}})\Aa f_{N_i}\to 0$ is in fact equivalent to $\Aa f=\lambda f$ (the conclusion), making the argument circular. Indeed, $(I-P_{F_{N_i}})\Aa f_{N_i}=\Aa f_{N_i}-\lambda_{N_i}f_{N_i}\stackrel{w}{\to}\Aa f-\lambda f$, so the claimed convergence to zero presupposes the conclusion.

failure_location.quote: in the second we used that $(\rm{Id}-\Pp_{\Ff_{N_i}})\Aa f_{N_i}\to 0$ by Assumption \ref{projection assumption}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\Aa$ is compact as an operator from $(D,\|\cdot\|_D)$ to $(F,\|\cdot\|_F)$. Then $f_{N_i}\stackrel{w}{\to}f$ in $D$ implies $\Aa f_{N_i}\to\Aa f$ strongly in $F$, which fills the gap. Alternatively, a fundamentally new argument is needed to handle unbounded non-compact generators.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem convergence eigenfunctions dictionary theorem is unproved: the claim that weak cluster points of normalized eigenpairs of $\Aa_N$ are eigenpairs of $\Aa$ is not established. Theorem convergence eigenfunctions joint theorem has the same gap through the identical step applied to the joint-limit sequence.
issues.title: Eigensystem dictionary-limit proof is circular: pointwise projection convergence applied to a varying sequence
issues.why_classification: A contained additional hypothesis (compactness) or a nontrivial new argument fills the gap and preserves the result for a large class of operators (e.g., generators of ergodic diffusions with spectral gap). This is more than a minor edit but avoids abandoning the theorem or changing its form substantially.
